_comment: The release lines of the third-party images the stack pins by digest (scripts/stack-lock-third-party.py THIRD_PARTY).
line        version prefix, in the tag's own spelling, that still gets fixes; 'newer upstream' means a newer tag in it
policy      the upstream page that says which lines get fixes (null: upstream publishes none)
recheck_by  ISO date: after it, the scheduled job opens an issue until someone re-reads the policy and moves the pin or the date
opt_in      true: a backend only an operator turns on; an issue only on a fixable CRITICAL or an EOSL base
A THIRD_PARTY row missing here is scanned all the same, as a default-on service with no line.

nginx.why: 1.30 is the stable line since 2026-04-14; nginx ships a new stable line each spring and the old one stops getting fixes

nats.why: two lines get patches (the latest minor and the one before); 2.15 shipped 2026-09-17 and a minor ships roughly every six months, so 2.14 ends with 2.16, expected around 2027-03-17

redis.why: DHI tag; line is the pinned tag, re-checked 6 months out
